title: Russia holds State Duma elections including in occupied parts of Ukraine
body:
On 18 September 2026, Russia began a three-day vote for State Duma seats, gubernatorial races and regional legislative assemblies. It was the first Duma election since President Vladimir Putin ordered the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, and voting took place in occupied parts of Ukraine, according to The Moscow Times.

Drone attacks disrupted the first day. In the Krasnodar region, a polling station was moved after drone damage broke its windows, according to Central Election Commission chief Ella Pamfilova. In occupied Luhansk, 14 polling stations briefly lost power after drones hit energy infrastructure, then switched to backup supplies. In Sochi, voters and election workers sought shelter during an air raid alert. A member of the Central Election Commission was reported killed in a drone attack in occupied Zaporizhzhia earlier that week.

Russian officials reported cyberattacks on the remote e-voting system, and Pamfilova warned of mobile internet disruptions. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin reported more than 350 incoming drones overnight, with at least 64 destroyed near the capital. Russia's Defense Ministry said it intercepted 629 Ukrainian drones overnight across Russia and Crimea.
